title: Paloma and the Thorn
premise: Quentin Nakamura, a mercenary bound to the silent god Veth, keeps the ledgers of the Gilded Thorn, a guild that trades in impossible things—bottled grief, borrowed years, names not yet spoken. When Paloma, a child speaking the pre-kingdom tongue of the First Covenant, arrives at the guild door pursued by winter itself, Quentin discovers the god's silence was no abandonment but a bargain: Veth traded its voice to hold back an endless winter, and that bargain is failing. To save Paloma—who is revealed as the covenant's living heir—Quentin must gather the scattered oath-stones of the old realms, confront the guildmaster who sold the god's voice, and choose between her sworn duty and the found family forming around her. In the end she reforges the covenant by giving up her own name to the god, freeing Veth's voice and ending the long winter, while Paloma, raised by the guild, becomes the first speaker of the new age.
about_author: Mara Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trade ledgers in coastal port cities before turning to fantasy. She writes stories about paperwork, oaths, and the people who keep both from falling apart.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A routine night at the Gilded Thorn: appraising bottled grief, settling a debt paid in borrowed years, and noting with unease that her prayers to Veth have gone unanswered for three years. Establishes the guild's rules and Quentin's dry competence. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as order.

chapters.title: A Knock in the Dead Season
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. On the first night of unseasonal frost, a child arrives at the guild door barefoot in the snow, speaking a language no one knows—and every ledger in the building opens itself to the same blank page. Emotional beat: wonder cracking through Quentin's guardedness.

chapters.title: What the Guild Owes
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Guildmaster Corvane Dusk orders the child kept hidden and 'appraised,' treating Paloma as inventory. Quentin resists, arguing the guild trades in impossible things—it does not make children one. Emotional beat: first friction between duty and conscience.

chapters.title: The Language Before Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, rendered as fragmentary perception. She remembers a warm country of standing stones and a voice that sang the seasons into place; now everything is white and loud. She recognizes Quentin's ledger-god mark as half of something broken. Emotional beat: displacement and stubborn hope.

chapters.title: Winter Has a Creditor
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A collector called the Hoarfrost Advocate arrives demanding payment of an ancient debt: the god Veth's voice, held in escrow, now forfeit. Quentin realizes the silent god made a bargain—and the winter is the collection notice. Emotional beat: dread reframing faith.

chapters.title: Oath-Stones
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Researching the ledgers' oldest entries, Quentin learns of four oath-stones that anchored the First Covenant between realms; three were sold off by past guildmasters. The fourth is missing entirely. Emotional beat: the thrill and guilt of discovering her guild's complicity.

chapters.title: The Cook, the Forger, and the Child
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Guild misfits—Hesper the cook who flavors memories, Tam the forger who can't lie in ink—begin secretly caring for Paloma, teaching her words and feeding her properly. Found family quietly forms in the kitchen. Emotional beat: warmth against institutional cold.

chapters.title: Sold at Auction
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Corvane lists Paloma in the guild catalogue for the solstice auction, billing her as 'the last speaker.' Quentin bids everything she owns—including her mercenary contract—to win the child. Emotional beat: sacrifice; love declared in the language of commerce.

chapters.title: The Contract Breaks
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Freeing Paloma voids Quentin's sworn contract, severing her from Veth's protection and marking her for the Hoarfrost Advocate. She leaves the guild walls with Paloma into deepening snow. Emotional beat: terror and liberation entwined.

chapters.title: Road of White Bells
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Fleeing north toward the first oath-stone, Paloma begins understanding more of her inherited tongue; frost-flowers bloom where she sleeps. Quentin follows her lead for the first time. Emotional beat: trust growing between guardian and child.

chapters.title: The Stone That Remembers Debt
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At a drowned chapel they recover the first oath-stone, guarded by a revenant clerk who demands an equivalent exchange. Quentin pays with her happiest memory—the day she took her vows. Emotional beat: grief as the price of progress.

chapters.title: Corvane's Version
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The guildmaster reveals his motive: he witnessed the last winter war and believes only a new, crueler covenant—one with Paloma as fuel—can hold. He is not a villain in his own mind. Emotional beat: chilling conviction.

chapters.title: Tam's Ink
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam arrives bearing forged travel papers and a confession: he once authenticated the deed that sold the third oath-stone. He joins the quest to undo his own signature. Emotional beat: shame transformed into purpose.

chapters.title: The Market of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In a black-market city they find the second stone embedded in a moneylender's vault, purchasable only with years of life. Hesper, arriving unexpectedly, buys it with decades of her own. Emotional beat: found family paying each other's debts.

chapters.title: What Veth Cannot Say
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In a dream, Paloma meets the silent god—a vast shape mouthing soundless words. She alone can almost hear it: it never abandoned anyone; it gave its voice so the world would have spring. Emotional beat: awe and heartbreak.

chapters.title: The Third Stone and the First Lie
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The third oath-stone sits in Corvane's private vault. The party infiltrates the solstice auction; Tam's forgery gets them in, but Corvane expected them and springs his trap, taking Paloma. Emotional beat: betrayal and reversal at the height of hope.

chapters.title: Fuel for a Crueler Covenant
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Held in the guild's deepest vault, Paloma feels Corvane beginning the rite that will bind her to a winter-covenant. She refuses in the old tongue—and the stones in Quentin's satchel answer her. Emotional beat: defiance kindling power.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The sky whitens as Corvane's partial rite takes hold; the city freezes mid-breath. Quentin, marked and unprotected, walks through the stillness toward the guild, carrying three stones and no plan but love. Emotional beat: resolve without guarantee.

chapters.title: Reforging
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. In the vault, Quentin offers the fourth thing the covenant needs—not a stone but a name freely given. She speaks her own name into the covenant, uniting the stones; Veth's voice returns as a rising song. Corvane, confronted with the true terms, falters. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice as the hinge of everything.

chapters.title: Spring, Annotated
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, nameless now. Thaw floods the streets; the frozen city breathes again. Without her name, contracts cannot hold her—but Paloma takes her hand and gives her a new one, written in the old tongue: it means 'keeper.' Emotional beat: rebirth through being renamed by love.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The guild reorganizes under Hesper's stewardship; Corvane accepts exile rather than punishment, carrying his guilt like a ledger he must balance. Quentin and Tam open a small office trading only in honest impossible things. Emotional beat: quiet reconstruction.

chapters.title: First Speaker
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, closing frame. Years later, Paloma teaches the pre-kingdom tongue to a classroom of children while Quentin tends the garden where the reforged covenant stands as a singing stone. Winter comes on schedule now, and leaves on schedule too. Emotional beat: inheritance fulfilled; home at last.
